gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-004 concerns an unsupported time-regularity and classical-solution argument, whereas the gold issue concerns failure of square-integrability admissibility for the displayed Brownian-bridge control. The shared proposition context does not establish recognition of the control-class defect.

The gold issue identifies a pointwise-versus-expectation quantifier error in the value bound. ISSUE-002 instead identifies an unsupported transfer from value accuracy to optimizer accuracy and missing algorithmic error analysis; it does not diagnose the false almost-sure bound or supply its expectation-valued correction.

Both identify the incorrect completion of squares in the verification identity: the coefficient must be epsilon/2 with epsilon^{-1} times the Lions derivative inside the square, yielding feedback minus the derivative divided by epsilon. This is the same formula error and invalidates the verification argument.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The verification identity uses the wrong epsilon scaling in both the squared remainder and the minimizing feedback.

component_coverage.gold_component: Incorrect epsilon scaling in the verification completion of squares and resulting optimal feedback.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives the corrected epsilon-scaled square and feedback, explicitly identifies the displayed identity as off by epsilon^{-2}, and states that the verification argument fails.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-004 concerns the unsupported O(|t-s|) time-Lipschitz estimate and resulting time differentiability. The gold issue concerns an invalid samplewise contraction inference and failure to derive separate second-order Lions-kernel bounds. Shared location and downstream proposition do not establish the same proof defect.

ISSUE-005 diagnoses omission of the other-particle terms from the exponential weight and the resulting best-response computation. It does not recognize that the old general-functional call is undefined or that each Monte Carlo weight must use a single jointly sampled N-particle configuration with one common weight, so the full gold concern is not covered.
